title: 1. Meaning of Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)

blocks.content: The Directive Principles constitute a comprehensive economic, social and political programme for a modern democratic State.

rows: Negative as they prohibit the State from doing certain things
Positive as they require the State to do certain things
Justiciable and legally enforceable by courts
Non-justiciable and not legally enforceable by courts
Aim at establishing political democracy in the country
Aim at establishing social and economic democracy
Promote the welfare of the individual (Individualistic)
Promote the welfare of the community (Socialistic)

items: DPSPs are non-justiciable, meaning courts cannot compel the government to implement them.
Article 37 explicitly declares that Directive Principles are fundamental in the governance of the country.
Fundamental Rights aim at establishing political democracy, whereas DPSPs aim at establishing social and economic democracy.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Directive Principles of State Policy are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution from Articles 36 to 51.
The framers of the Constitution borrowed this concept from the Irish Constitution of 1937, which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described these principles as 'novel features' of the Indian Constitution.
DPSPs denote the ideals that the State should keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws.
The primary objective of DPSPs is to establish social and economic democracy and achieve a welfare state.
